info.name: PAIGS WildID -- API
info.description:
Manual test collection for the PAIGS WildID backend.

Updated 2026-09-24: added 'Configuration' (GET/PUT /config) and 'Rerun (Configuration subsystem)' (POST /runs/{id}/rerun, including its auto_execute option) folders, on top of the earlier 'End-to-end (Orchestration)' folder covering POST /runs/{id}/execute.

Setup:
1. From backend/, run: uvicorn app.main:app --reload
2. Import the PAIGS environment (postman/PAIGS.postman_environment.json) alongside this collection and select it.
3. 'Happy path' and 'Errors' cover Stage 0 (Import) only -- run 'Happy path' top to bottom first, it captures run_id into the environment. 'Errors' can be run independently, except 'Patch run - rejects empty label', which reuses run_id.
4. 'End-to-end (Orchestration)', 'Configuration', and 'Rerun (Configuration subsystem)' each publish their own reference database version and create their own runs -- run each folder top to bottom, in its own pass, rather than interleaving requests across folders (they publish reference databases under different version strings specifically so they don't collide with each other, but a partial/out-of-order run within a folder can still leave its own captured environment variables stale).

Test data lives in postman/test-data/ (copies of backend/tests/fixtures/*.ab1, a plain-text file for exercising the extension-rejection case, and reference.fasta -- a single-entry reference database whose sequence is 3100.ab1's own real trimmed output, extracted from backend/tests/test_api_execute.py, guaranteeing a clean 100%-identity BLAST hit wherever it's published).

Publishes a one-entry reference database whose sequence is 3100.ab1's own real trimmed output (see postman/test-data/reference.fasta) -- guarantees a clean, unambiguous 100%-identity/coverage BLAST hit for the requests below, so this exercises Stage 9-11 against a real match rather than a fabricated one.

request.description: A fresh run (a run can only be executed once -- see 'already executed' below), created now that a matching reference database is active.

request.description: Runs every stage end to end: format_check, ab1_extraction, sanity_check, trim, orientation (skipped -- single-read path), consensus (skipped), usability_check, fasta, blast, identification, report. Always 200 -- the biological/QC outcome is data on the Run/Stage response, not an HTTP error.
Confirms the clean match against the published reference entry.

request.description: Stage 11's output is a path, not the PDF bytes themselves (see claude/stage-11-status.md) -- the file itself lives on the server's disk at report_path.

request.description: Every stage_type has a row, including the two skipped ones (orientation, consensus) on this single-read run.

item.name: Create run - two real unrelated reads (3100 + 3730)

request.description: 3100.ab1 and 3730.ab1 are confirmed-unrelated real fixtures (see claude/stage-5-6-status.md) -- both pass format_check/sanity_check/trim individually, but genuinely share no overlap.

item.name: Execute run - two unrelated reads stop at orientation (no overlap)

request.description: Stage 5's 'flags for review rather than guessing' path on real data, no synthetic reads needed -- maps to Run.status=failed since the Run.status enum has no REVIEW_REQUIRED state (see claude/orchestration-status.md).
Consensus never runs once orientation finds no overlap -- recorded as skipped, not failed.

The default admin account is seeded automatically on first login attempt (app.auth.service.ensure_default_admin) -- no setup step needed. Credentials come from PAIGS_ADMIN_EMAIL/PAIGS_ADMIN_PASSWORD, falling back to the documented prototype defaults below if unset. Uses OAuth2's standard username/password form fields (not JSON) -- the same shape Swagger UI's "Authorize" button submits. Captures admin_token for every admin-only request below.
Confirms the bearer token actually identifies the caller -- every authenticated endpoint in the API accepts this same header.

The admin's only account-management feature for now, per the product decision: create an invited user and hand back a one-time temporary password. Email delivery is deliberately stubbed (app.auth.email_stub) -- delivered is always false, and the admin is expected to copy temporary_password from this response and share it with the invited user directly, exactly like a real admin would.

exec: pm.test('email delivery is stubbed, not actually sent', () => pm.expect(body.email.delivered).to.eql(false));

request.description: Proves the credentials the admin copied out of the invite response above actually work -- exactly the flow the invited user follows after the admin shares them out-of-band.
